text.tspan: Hoisting and the Temporal Dead Zone
Declarations are registered before the code runs. What differs is whether you may touch them yet.
No error, just a confusing value, which is
why modern code does not use var.
Hoisted but NOT initialized. The gap between
the two is the Temporal Dead Zone: the name
Fully hoisted, body and all. A function stored
in a let or const follows that variable's rules
instead, so it is NOT callable early.
The practical rule is simple: const by default, let when you must reassign, var never. Declare things before you use them and
the TDZ never fires. Note that const freezes the BINDING, not the value: the contents of a const object can still change.
